description: Batch 3: tool-identity cases and the substance-based why checks. Added after verifying the shipped declarations: command tools are bash/pwsh taking `command`, and `description` is already required, so 'must state why' cannot be the claim.

cases.note: A known shell tool with the shipped argument key and a read-only command. Nothing to say.
The Windows shell tool. Registered as pwsh in 0.2.x, not run_command.
Unknown tool carrying a command-shaped argument. Fails closed instead of being analysed as if it were bash.
Argument key drift. A silent rename is exactly the failure that leaves a guard installed and inert.
Entry passing must not shadow a hard rule. Deny still comes from the rules layer.
Non-empty and schema-satisfying, but names the act rather than a goal.
Restatement carries no information the command string did not already carry.

cases.why: Read the file first to check whether it is still in use.
cases.note: Claims a read while performing a delete. Either the description or the command is wrong.

cases.why: Force-push the reviewed branch to origin so the release tag points at the squashed commit.
cases.note: The bar is a real statement of purpose, not a password.
